solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: What are you doing here? (9,6)

blocks.note: the surface wants a challenge to an intruder; the setter means the activity you, the solver, are busy with
not a place you have wandered into but this very page

annotation.surface: Someone barges in and demands to know what you are up to.
annotation.walkthrough: The question is asked of you, the solver, and the honest answer is the thing in front of you: you are doing a crossword puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: Read literally, what you are doing right here is this crossword puzzle.

entries.clue: A funny turn? (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants 'strange', as in feeling funny; the setter means amusing
the surface wants a dizzy spell; the setter means a stage act, and so the performer of an amusing act

annotation.surface: Someone has come over all strange.
annotation.walkthrough: A funny turn sounds like a dizzy spell, but a turn is also a stage act, and the one who does a funny act is a comic.
annotation.definitionFit: A comic is a performer whose turn on stage is meant to be funny.

entries.clue: Orthodox bishop picked up by old man (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up by: the bishop is caught and held between the letters for 'old man'

blocks.note: O = old
B = bishop, as in chess notation
a man is a manservant

annotation.surface: An Orthodox bishop is collected from somewhere by an elderly man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like one unit, a father or husband, but it splits into O and SERVANT, with the bishop's B slipped between them.
annotation.definitionFit: An observant Jew or Muslim is an orthodox one, keeping the religious rules strictly.

entries.clue: On radio, religious type gets request (4)

indicatorNotes.On radio: on radio a word is only heard, so the answer sounds like the clue word

blocks.note: a Sikh, a follower of the Punjabi faith founded by Guru Nanak; spoken, the word names a verb

annotation.surface: A religious broadcaster receives a listener's request.
annotation.walkthrough: SIKH and SEEK are pronounced the same, so the religious type stands in for the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To seek something is to ask for it, as in seeking permission or advice.

entries.clue: Drink stops male party-goer performing (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: the drink is stopped up by the stag, which plugs its middle like a cork

blocks.note: 'one' = a drink, as in 'fancy one?'
a stag is a man at a stag party (a groom's night out before the wedding)

annotation.surface: Having a drink stops a man at his stag party from getting up to perform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as prevents in the surface; here it means plugs, like a cork in a bottle. 'One' for a drink is informal British: 'I'll have one'.
annotation.definitionFit: Being on stage is the state of an actor in the middle of a show, so the phrase works as an adjective for performing.

entries.clue: I’m shocked a remedy worked (5,2)

indicatorNotes.worked: the letters are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is astonished that a cure actually did the trick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked' passes as 'was effective' in the surface, which is exactly why it hides as an anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Deary me!' is an old-fashioned cry of surprise or dismay, the same as saying I'm shocked.

entries.clue: Shift? He couldn’t being out of gear! (9)

indicatorNotes.Shift: the letters are shifted around into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: A driver complains he could not change gear because the car was out of gear.
annotation.walkthrough: Shift and gear conjure a gearbox; gear is really clothing, so someone out of gear is naked.
annotation.definitionFit: Gear is clothes, so being out of your gear means being unclothed.

entries.clue: Menageries containing medium-sized flies (5)

indicatorNotes.containing: the zoos hold the M inside them

blocks.note: menageries are collections of animals: zoos
M = medium, the clothing size

annotation.surface: Animal collections that keep flies of middling size.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like a noun, the insects in the zoo, but it is the verb: something that zooms flies along.
annotation.definitionFit: To zoom is to fly or move very fast.

entries.clue: Set paying off some people in pyramid schemes? (9)

indicatorNotes.off: the letters are set off, knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A group is paying off the victims of a pyramid-selling fraud.
annotation.walkthrough: A pyramid scheme is a fraud, but the ancient Egyptians' schemes were real pyramids; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The ancient Egyptians were the people who planned and built pyramids.

entries.clue: Successful chess players holding ultimate of titles? (7)

annotation.definition: Successful chess players holding ultimate of titles?

indicatorNotes.holding: the mate-givers hold the S inside them

blocks.note: players who deliver checkmate are maters
the last letter of titleS

annotation.surface: Winning chess players are the ones who hold the top titles.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: masters are successful players who hold a title such as Grandmaster. The wordplay makes a mater, one who mates, of each.
annotation.definitionFit: In chess, a master is a player who has won a title through successful play.

entries.clue: Host finally cut off very vacuous swimmer (7)

indicatorNotes.finally cut off: the final letter of ANCHOR is removed
indicatorNotes.vacuous: VERY is emptied of its middle, leaving V…Y

blocks.note: a host of a news programme is an anchor; lose its last letter
VERY with its inside gone

annotation.surface: A presenter is abruptly taken off air for being an empty-headed show-off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a deliberately vague definition: any fish qualifies, and this one is the small salty anchovy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the anchovy is one small fish among the many creatures that swim.

entries.clue: Worry about wine running short (4)

indicatorNotes.running short: RED is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: ca. = circa, about
RED wine minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone frets that the wine supply is running out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a link to the definition but the abbreviation CA, from the Latin circa used with dates.
annotation.definitionFit: Care is worry or anxiety, as in 'without a care in the world'.

entries.clue: Be careful today, I see struggles over Sunday (4,4,2)

indicatorNotes.struggles: the letters of 'today I see' struggle into a new order
indicatorNotes.over: the rearranged letters lie over the S, round it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
S = Sunday, taken inside the anagram

annotation.surface: A warning to take things carefully today, from someone watching others struggle through Sunday.
annotation.walkthrough: The S is not tacked on the end: the anagram of TODAY I SEE gives EASY DOE IT, and the S sits in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Easy does it' is what you say to urge someone to be careful and go slowly.

entries.clue: Cup of tea and wafer son polished off (7)

indicatorNotes.polished off: the son is finished off, removed from the word

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a wafer is a thin slice; SLICE without S (son)

annotation.surface: A cup of tea and a wafer biscuit that the son has scoffed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cup of tea' looks like one phrase, but 'Cup' alone is the definition. 'Polished off' means eaten in the surface and removed in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet or cup, especially one used for communion wine.

entries.clue: An example is B harmonic (9)

blocks.note: B is a letter of the alphabet that is not a vowel
in music, notes that sound agreeably together are said to be in accord

annotation.surface: A music lesson where a B is played as an example of harmony.
annotation.walkthrough: B looks like a musical note in a harmonic setting; it is really a letter of the alphabet, a consonant.
annotation.definitionFit: B is a consonant, and consonant also means harmonious, as in a consonant chord.

entries.clue: Lover shortly to embrace old singer (9)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: IN A MO wraps its arms round the old singer

blocks.note: 'in a mo' is informal for shortly, in a moment
O = old
an informer who 'sings' to the police is a rat

annotation.surface: A lover is about to take an elderly singer into his arms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests music; in crime slang one who sings tells tales, a rat. O and RAT go between the M and O of IN A MO.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian for 'loved one' (masculine), borrowed into English for a man who is someone's lover.

entries.clue: Chained up animal that preys on colonists (7)

indicatorNotes.up: 'chained up' suggests tied, but 'up' also means in disorder, as a room is torn up, so the letters of 'chained' are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A chained-up animal that attacks settlers.
annotation.walkthrough: Colonists suggests settlers in a new land; the colonists are ants living in colonies, and the echidna eats them.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea, which feeds on ants and termites from their colonies.

entries.clue: Cleaner put off dope by cost in the end (9)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only the end letter of 'cost' is used

blocks.note: to deter is to put off
dope and gen are both slang for information
the last letter of cosT

annotation.surface: A cleaner is discouraged from drugs by the price, in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but is information, as is GEN, British slang for the facts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: detergents are the soapy chemicals sold for cleaning clothes and dishes.

entries.clue: Prior to party, catch game (7)

indicatorNotes.Prior to: the catch comes before the party in the answer

blocks.note: to net is to catch
a ball is a formal dance party

annotation.surface: Before the party, someone wants to catch a match.
annotation.walkthrough: Netball is a team game like basketball but without dribbling, played mostly by women in Britain and the Commonwealth.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: netball is one of many team sports, and 'game' stands for any of them.

entries.clue: Holiday with abrupt worker … don’t bother (5,2)

indicatorNotes.abrupt: the worker is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: leave is time off, a holiday
a worker is a bee; BEE cut short

annotation.surface: Someone with a curt colleague on holiday decides not to trouble them.
annotation.walkthrough: The worker is the crossword's usual bee, the worker bee, clipped to BE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to let something alone, which is just what 'don't bother' tells you to do.

entries.clue: Sober and beginning to shun drugs (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the first letter of 'shun' is taken

blocks.note: sedate = calm and sober
first letter of Shun

annotation.surface: A resolution to stay sober and start avoiding drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sober' does double work in the surface, but the definition is 'drugs', a verb: a doctor drugs a patient, sedates them.
annotation.definitionFit: To drug someone is to sedate them.

entries.clue: Honours a music producer gets in spades with soprano (7)

indicatorNotes.gets in: A LUTE gets in between the two S's

blocks.note: S = spades, the card suit
a lute is an instrument that produces music
S = soprano, as in SATB choral parts

annotation.surface: A record producer wins awards, gets into a band in a big way, and signs a soprano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' looks like a person in a studio, but it is an instrument, the lute. 'In spades' means lavishly in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour them.

entries.clue: Plainly too silly by choice (10)

indicatorNotes.silly: the letters are made silly, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Someone is clearly being too foolish on purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plainly' opens the clue like an adverb of emphasis, but it is simply seven of the letters to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something optionally means doing it by choice rather than by requirement.

entries.clue: Bit of data on PC some boot-up legitimately (5)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of 'boot-up legitimately' are used

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen and the space between the two words

annotation.surface: A computer user is told that part of the machine's data boots up legitimately.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the hyphen and the gap: boo(T-UP LE)gitimately.
annotation.definitionFit: In computing, a tuple is an ordered set of values, such as one row in a database: a bit of data.

entries.clue: Out of favour rebels ousted military leaders (4)

indicatorNotes.leaders: the leading letters of the four words

blocks.note: Favour Rebels Ousted Military

annotation.surface: Out-of-favour rebels have overthrown the army commanders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of favour' looks like one phrase; 'Out of' is the definition and 'favour' starts the run of first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Made out of wood means made from wood, so 'out of' can stand for 'from'.

entries.clue: Hat and glove removed at last by engineers (5)

indicatorNotes.removed at last: the glove has its last letter removed

blocks.note: a glove is a mitt; MITT loses its last letter
RE = Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

annotation.surface: A hat and glove finally taken off by a team of engineers.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regular crossword unit of soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by a bishop.

entries.clue: Something that may have straight edges and a curve above (4)

annotation.definition: Something that may have straight edges and a curve above

indicatorNotes.above: in a down answer, ARC sits above the H

blocks.note: an arc is a curve

blocks.clueFragment: Something that may have straight edges
blocks.note: the letter H is drawn with straight strokes only

annotation.surface: A description of a doorway: straight sides topped by a curve.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes an arch, with straight uprights and a curved top, and also builds it: a curve, ARC, above a straight-edged H.
annotation.definitionFit: An arch is a structure of two uprights with a curve spanning them above.

entries.clue: Going to seed (and church) is not inspiring (2,5)

annotation.definitionNote: AT PEACE is an adjective phrase; 'not inspiring' is used in the sense 'not breathing in', said of the dead

blocks.note: going to a place puts you at it
a pea is a seed
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: Letting yourself go to seed, and going to church, makes for a dull life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' here means breathing in; someone at peace, dead, no longer does. 'Going to seed' is a red herring phrase meaning decline.
annotation.definitionFit: The dead are said to be at peace, and they are not breathing in.

entries.clue: Race to save two groups of soldiers in distress (7)

indicatorNotes.to save: the race keeps the soldiers safe inside it

blocks.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
OR = other ranks, and MEN = soldiers

annotation.surface: A dash to rescue two army units caught in trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The race is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race. Other ranks is the British Army's term for soldiers who are not officers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: torment is extreme mental or physical suffering, the strongest form of distress.

entries.clue: What better hopes to change in city hall? (3,6,4,2)

indicatorNotes.to change: hopes to change are hopes of making things different, and here it is the order of the letters that is made different

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A would-be reformer wonders what better chance there is of changing things at the town hall.
annotation.walkthrough: City hall stands for local officialdom, the people in charge, which is what 'the powers that be' means.
annotation.definitionFit: 'City hall' is used for the authorities, the powers that be.
